learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of React components and JSX.
Compose reusable interfaces from smaller components.
Identify the basic structure of a React application.

activities.title: React App Anatomy
activities.instruction: Click each part to explore its role in a React application.

content.concept: A React application is built from components that return JSX and are rendered through an application entry point.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: A reusable UI building block that can contain its own logic and presentation.
A syntax extension that lets React components describe UI using HTML-like syntax.
Inputs passed from a parent component to a child component.
The part of the application that starts rendering the React component tree.

activities.title: JSX Explorer
activities.instruction: Identify the JavaScript and JSX parts of a React component.

content.concept: JSX allows developers to describe UI with HTML-like syntax while embedding JavaScript expressions inside curly braces.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Describes an element that React can render.
Embeds a JavaScript expression inside JSX.
Returns the JSX that the component renders.

activities.title: Component Composition Builder
activities.instruction: Compose a page from smaller reusable React components.

content.concept: Component composition builds complex interfaces by combining smaller components such as Header, Navigation, Content, and Footer.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: React Rendering Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the basic flow from a React component to the rendered interface.

content.concept: React evaluates the component tree, creates the corresponding UI representation, and updates the browser when the rendered output changes.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
